note: Ratchet for `scripts/loc-metrics.py`. Every number below is lines of git-tracked source, classified by the lexer in `scripts/lib/loc_classify.py`. They may only go DOWN — raising a limit to make a build green defeats the point of measuring, so a rise fails the gate. When a rise is deliberate, run `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline` and commit the new file in the SAME commit that grew the tree. Generated files (`@generated` / `DO NOT EDIT` in the header) are measured but excluded from these limits, because appending a wire kind must never fail a size gate. The `*.comment` numbers are measured and diffed but NOT gated: a gate that makes deleting documentation the cheapest way to go green is pointed at the wrong thing.
measured: 2026-08-06 on `refactor/decompose-god-classes-#213` (Plan 11 phase 4, issue #213). java.main.code RISES 60,815 -> 60,841 (+26) and that rise is the phase's finding rather than a regression: extracting a reusable primitive costs more lines than the short duplicated loops it absorbs. HexKeyedStore is ~95 lines replacing ~72 across two stores; SignedGossipRelay ~35 replacing four copies of an 11-line flood; WorldIds ~12 replacing seven copies of a 3-line helper; Json ~95 replacing ten hand-concatenated replies that were already one line per field. Reuse extraction here improved the Java without shrinking it — it deleted three divergent JSON escapes (one of which emitted invalid output), unified a path-traversal guard that existed in two versions, and removed two dead accessors the structural report named, which is why fixtures/structure/budget.json tightened 136 -> 134 in the same branch. Nothing was cut to reach this number: java.main.comment RISES 200 in the same measurement. The other two languages fall, because their duplication was one idea written several ways rather than a primitive waiting to be named: rust.main.code -42 (the ENFORCEMENT table behind three const fn constructors) and ts.code -23 (four identical button components behind one variant). The ratchet is a whole-tree measurement and does not compose across parallel branches, so this branch reads red in isolation and green in the tree it is going into; re-stamped downward at integration, where it merges with #210, #211, #212 and #214 to java.main.code 60,234.
